description: Create a private S3 bucket for this application now, while the project is still being written, so uploads are built and tested against real storage instead of the container's disk, which is wiped on every deploy. A later deploy gives the running app the same bucket. Safe to call twice. Only for a project that stores uploads or generated files: skip it otherwise, and skip it when the project already has a storage key of its own (an AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID in .env that is not ours, or a service the user named, such as Cloudinary or UploadThing): the answer is a 409 own_storage. It counts against the plan's bucket allowance; a 402 storage_limit is not a rate limit, so do not retry, say what it says and let the user choose. If the call is refused or blocked, do not look for another route: tell the user. The key is not returned: call `storage_env_to_file` to put it in .env. Addressing is path style, which current AWS SDKs and boto3 choose by themselves for this bucket's name, so existing code that reads those variables works as it is; in new JavaScript code set forcePathStyle: true anyway. A browser can upload straight to the bucket with a presigned PUT URL. Tell the user what was created and on which account.
name: storage_create
title: Create the application's file storage now
